title: Filtered admissible blowup system and completion-compatible closed fibres
statement: Let $(A,I)$ be a henselian pair with $I$ finitely generated [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology], let $A'=\widehat A$ be its $I$-adic completion [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], and put $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$, $X'=\operatorname{Spec}A'$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], $U=X\setminus V(I)$, and $U'=X'\setminus V(IA')$. Let $\mathscr J(A,I)$ be the set of finitely generated ideals $J\subseteq A$ with $V(J)=V(I)$, and for $J\in\mathscr J(A,I)$ write $B_J=\operatorname{Bl}_J(X)$ [def-nagata-affine-blowup] and $Z_J=B_J\times_X\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Order these blowups by domination: $J\preceq K$ when there is an $X$-morphism $B_K\to B_J$. Then this is a filtered preorder, and the restriction $j_J:U\hookrightarrow B_J$ is a schematically dense open immersion (the map $\mathcal O_{B_J}\to j_{J*}\mathcal O_U$ is injective) [lemma-nagata-admissible-blowup-over-open] for every $J$. Extension of ideals along $A\to A'$ induces an order-preserving cofinal identification of $\mathscr J(A,I)$ with the corresponding full-support admissible ideals for $(A',IA')$. For every $J$ and $m\geq1$, the canonical map on Rees powers induces compatible isomorphisms $(J^n/I^mJ^n)\xrightarrow{\sim}((JA')^n/I^m(JA')^n)$ for all $n\geq0$, and hence identifies the closed fibre $Z_J$ with the closed fibre of $\operatorname{Bl}_{JA'}(X')$ over $A'/IA'$.

source.place: Expose XX section 4.4, printed pp.373--374: definition of admissible J, filtered preorder, full-support uniqueness, and final Note on isomorphisms modulo powers of I.

proof.text: The ideal I is an index, so the system is nonempty. Identities and composition of morphisms over Spec A give reflexivity and transitivity. If J,K are indices, their product is finitely generated and V(JK)=V(J) union V(K)=V(I). By [lem-per-blowup-domination-ideal-factorization], with exponent one, JK=J*K=K*J gives maps from the product blowup to both blowups. Thus the preorder is filtered.

source.place: Expose XX section 4.4, printed pp.373--374, admissible full-support blowups and final Note; quotient argument in XX 2.4.3, printed p.364.

proof.text: Because $J$ has support $V(I)$, its ideal sheaf is the unit ideal on $U$; [thm-nagata-global-blowup-complement] identifies the blowup over $U$ with $U$. By [thm-nagata-blowup-principalizes-center], on $B_J$ the extended ideal $J\mathcal O_{B_J}$ is locally generated by a non-zero-divisor $a$. Its zero locus is exactly the inverse image of $V(J)$, so on each such affine neighbourhood $W=\operatorname{Spec}C$ the preserved open is $D(a)$. The restriction $C\to C[1/a]$ is injective: an element in its kernel is killed by $a^t$, and repeated injectivity of multiplication by $a$ makes it zero. Apply this on a basis of affine neighbourhoods to obtain injectivity of $\mathcal O_{B_J}\to j_{J*}\mathcal O_U$. No density of $U$ in $X$ is assumed. In Lean the terminal affine chart identifies the global ideal-sheaf blowup with the specified affine blowup; [lem-pc-invertible-ideal-complement-schematic-dominance] supplies the injectivity after principalization. Finite generation makes the preserved open quasi-compact, so schematic dominance gives injectivity on every open.

source.place: Expose XX section 4.4, printed pp.373--374, admissible full-support blowups and final Note; quotient argument in XX 2.4.3, printed p.364.

proof.text: For every $N\geq1$, [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-mod-power] identifies $A/I^N$ with $A'/I^NA'$ by the canonical map. Consequently extension and contraction biject the ideals containing $I^N$ and $I^NA'$: both are simply inverse images of the same ideals of this quotient ring. These bijections preserve inclusions and reflect equality. If an ideal $H\prime\subseteq A'$ is finitely generated and contains $I^NA'$, lift its finitely many generators modulo $I^NA'$ to $a_1,\ldots,a_t\in A$. The ideal $H=(a_1,\ldots,a_t)+I^N$ is finitely generated, extends to $H\prime$, and is its contraction. Conversely a finitely generated $H\supseteq I^N$ extends to a finitely generated ideal and is recovered by contraction. The constructions for different $N$ agree because they are extension and contraction. For full-support ideals [lem-weil-pbc-fg-ideal-radical-power] supplies power bounds on both sides; extension preserves these bounds, and contraction reflects $H^s\subseteq I$ by the quotient comparison for $N=1$. Hence extension gives a bijection between the two sets of full-support indices.

source.place: Expose XX section 4.4, printed pp.373--374, admissible full-support blowups and final Note; quotient argument in XX 2.4.3, printed p.364.

proof.text: Apply [lem-per-blowup-domination-ideal-factorization] to two full-support indices $J,K$. If $B_K\to B_J$ exists, write $K^n=JL$ with $L$ finitely generated. Extension preserves products and powers, so $(KA')^n=(JA')(LA')$ and the criterion gives domination after completion. Conversely, if domination exists after completion, the criterion gives $(KA')^n=(JA')L\prime$ with $L\prime$ finitely generated. Choose $r\geq1$ with $I^r\subseteq K$, using [lem-weil-pbc-fg-ideal-radical-power]. Since $(KA')^n\subseteq L\prime$, the ideal $L\prime$ contains $I^{rn}A'$, so Step 3 descends it to a finitely generated ideal $L$ containing $I^{rn}$. Both $K^n$ and $JL$ contain a power of $I$: for the latter use $I^t\subseteq J$ and $I^{rn}\subseteq L$. Their extensions are equal, so the quotient comparison of Step 3 reflects their equality. Thus $K^n=JL$, and the criterion gives $B_K\to B_J$. Extension is therefore an isomorphism of preorders, in particular order-preserving and cofinal.

source.place: Expose XX section 4.4, printed pp.373--374, admissible full-support blowups and final Note; quotient argument in XX 2.4.3, printed p.364.

proof.text: Fix J and choose r>=1 with I^r contained in J by [lem-weil-pbc-fg-ideal-radical-power]. For L=J^n one has I^(rn) contained in L and I^(m+rn) contained in I^m L. The canonical semilinear map L -> LA-prime descends to L/I^m L -> LA-prime/(IA-prime)^m LA-prime. Membership in the submodule I^m times the top submodule of L is exactly membership of the underlying element in the ambient ideal I^m L. Injectivity follows from the extension/contraction equality for I^m L proved in Step 3, using [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-mod-power]. For surjectivity, approximate an element y of LA-prime by the image of a in A modulo I^(m+rn)A-prime. Their difference lies in (I^m L)A-prime, so a belongs to L by the contraction equality for L. Its residue class lifts the class of y. This also handles n=0 with L=A, without requiring a positive degree. The resulting additive equivalence has exactly the prescribed formula on every representative.

source.place: Expose XX section 4.4, printed pp.373--374, admissible full-support blowups and final Note; quotient argument in XX 2.4.3, printed p.364.

proof.text: A polynomial in the Rees ring belongs to the ideal extended from I^m exactly when each degree-n coefficient belongs to I^m J^n: the forward implication applies coefficient linear maps, and the reverse sums its finitely many monomials. Hence the degreewise quotient comparisons in Step 5 prove bijectivity of the canonical map of Rees reductions as an ordinary ring map. Its formula on representatives also pins the grading. Apply [lem-per-blowup-closed-fiber-of-rees-reduction] with m=1 and the canonical residue-ring isomorphism of Step 3. This gives the specified closed-fibre isomorphism and both projection identities. The new lemma contains only the geometric Proj base-change step of the previous plan, with no completion, index or domination assertion.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q137-60a17611e (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, the one new node, every cited statement and ILO XX 4.4 (printed pp.373-374) in full. The source is Gabber's non-Noetherian letter: 'When V(J)⊂V(J′), J≤J′ iff J′^n=JK for some n>0 and ideal K' and 'isomorphism of the preordered set of admissible J's of full support', and its Note gives ⊕J^n→⊕J^nA′ as an isomorphism mod I^m. The item statement matches these and is unchanged by the delivery. New node lem-per-blowup-domination-ideal-factorization is the p.373 criterion specialised to equal radicals, with the same direction. Taking L finitely generated is valid: keep only the finitely many coefficients in expressions for the generators of K^n. I checked it is true for arbitrary rings. ⇐: J·O_{B_K} is a factor of the invertible ideal K^n·O_{B_K}, so it is invertible and the universal property gives the map. ⇒: U is schematically dense in B_K, so J·O_{B_K} is invertible; twisting O(d) and comparing graded ideals in high degree gives K^{N+d+e}=J·L₁K^e. I tested it on unit ideals, nilpotent ideals, (t²) vs (t) in k[t], and (x,y) vs (x,y²) in k[x,y], where neither blowup dominates the other and no power factorisation exists. It is statement-only, self-contained, cites its definitions and has six recorded searches of all kinds. It is not a duplicate (I searched the DAG for domination, power factorisation and admissible/completion nodes) and does not restate a clause of the item. Steps: Step 1 uses the radical-power leaf and the new node with n=1 and the product JK, so the preorder is filtered. Step 2: U is quasi-compact so the blowup is admissible; principalisation gives a local non-zero-divisor a with U∩W=D(a); the map C→C_a is injective on a basis of opens, and no density of U in X is assumed. Step 3: the completion-mod-power leaf gives A/I^N≅A′/I^NA′; ideals containing these powers correspond, finitely generated generators lift, and contraction reflects H^s⊆I modulo I. Step 4: (KA′)^n⊆L′ forces L′⊇I^{rn}A′, so L′ descends and equality is reflected; this gives an order isomorphism. Step 5: kernels of the canonical quotient isomorphisms, with n=0 consistent. Step 6: a graded Rees isomorphism plus Proj base change along A→A/I identifies the closed fibres. Accepted tool uses: thm-nagata-blowup-principalizes-center and lemma-nagata-relative-proj-base-change-arbitrary, both generic. Notes only: the Nagata results are stated for the global blowup and applied to the affine Proj, which is the convention elsewhere in the DAG; the citations.json named in the report is not in the commit. No fixes were made.
